first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent it, so I made a cup of tea and read it properly. The opening is warm and respectful, and 'It closes with what Australian couples need to know about marrying in Samoa, or bringing these customs into a wedding at home' told me the practical part was coming. I read the lot. The middle spends a long time on fine mats and museums, but the paragraphs are short and easy on the iPad.

journey.section: Samoan wedding traditions start with family
journey.quote: The best first step is a simple one: ask both families what they expect.
journey.reaction: Very sensible, and it doesn't make me feel silly for wanting to ask the other parents first. That's a conversation we'll be having.

journey.section: 2. The families meet: orators and formal speeches
journey.quote: Couples often ask who pays for a Samoan wedding. In many families, the cost and the work are shared across the aiga on both sides, with relatives contributing food, gifts and time.
journey.reaction: Now this matters to me, since I'm paying half. Good to know the other family may contribute food and gifts rather than money, so we can talk it through before anyone assumes.

journey.section: 3. Fine mats ('ie toga) and gifts between families
journey.quote: Te Papa's collection holds an 1800s example woven from pandanus with red feathers.
journey.reaction: Lovely, but it's a museum note, not something I need for the wedding. There's a lot of this in the mats section and I started skimming.

journey.section: 3. Fine mats ('ie toga) and gifts between families
journey.quote: For planning, treat heirloom mats as irreplaceable. Give the presentation unhurried time and a sheltered, dignified space, and agree handling, display and transport with the family, not with suppliers.
journey.reaction: That's the useful bit. If those mats are coming on a plane, I want to know who's carrying them and that they're insured.

journey.section: 5. Extended family and the village at Samoan weddings
journey.quote: Guests should follow the village's lead: remove shoes when entering a fale, and do not stand while elders are seated.
journey.reaction: Good manners, I'm glad to be told. But my mother can't sit on a floor mat or get her shoes off easily. Will there be chairs for older guests? It doesn't say.

journey.section: 6. Samoan wedding attire: what the bride and groom wear
journey.quote: A short dress note in the guest pack saves everyone guessing.
journey.reaction: Practical. I'd want that for our side of the family, who won't know what to wear to church over there.

journey.section: 8. The wedding feast and the umu
journey.quote: For a destination wedding, ask early whether your venue allows an umu on the grounds, or whether the family will cook off site and bring the food in.
journey.reaction: Exactly the kind of question I wouldn't have thought to ask. Underlined for my husband.

journey.section: 9. What UNESCO says about the 'ie Samoa
journey.quote: It is Samoa's only element on that list.
journey.reaction: Interesting, but I've already read a whole section about mats. This felt like the same thing again before I got to the part I actually needed.

journey.section: 10. Weddings in Samoa: getting married as an Australian
journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller advice for Samoa is "Exercise normal safety precautions", updated 5 August 2026, with an ongoing dengue outbreak since 2025.
journey.reaction: Reassuring that it's normal precautions and dated. But a dengue outbreak, with my elderly mother coming? I'd want to know what that means for older guests and what cover they need.

journey.section: 10. Weddings in Samoa: getting married as an Australian
journey.quote: Cyclone season runs from November to April, though storms can occur year-round, and earthquakes and tsunamis can occur.
journey.reaction: Honest, thank you. So what happens to our deposits if a cyclone cancels the wedding? That's the first thing my husband will ask.

journey.quote: Check every guest's passport expiry when invitations go out.
journey.reaction: Good, simple advice. Half our relatives will have expired passports.

journey.quote: Couples who marry in Samoa tend to choose Upolu or Savai'i, the two main islands, and plan the family ceremony and the feast around the island they pick.
journey.reaction: Nothing here or anywhere on how you get between the islands, how long transfers take, or whether older or less mobile guests can manage. That's my biggest worry and it isn't touched.

journey.quote: You can't register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law; talk to a lawyer to confirm.
journey.reaction: Good that they send you to a lawyer rather than pretending to know. And the list of questions for the registry is very helpful, I'd print that.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for venue, travel, vendors and guest rooms, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, with the fee and inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: That's the sentence I was looking for. One person, Australian dollars, my time zone, the fee in writing. It doesn't say who looks after us on the ground in Samoa or how deposits are protected, but it's the right start.

unanswered_questions: If we pay deposits to venues or suppliers in Samoa, is that money protected, and what happens if a cyclone forces us to postpone?
Are contracts with Samoan suppliers in English, and are all quotes in Australian dollars?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am Apia time? Is anyone from your side on the ground?
How would elderly or less mobile guests cope with the flight, transfers between Upolu and Savai'i, and sitting in a fale? Can chairs be arranged?
What travel insurance and medical cover should older guests have for Samoa, given the dengue outbreak?
Who is the Wedded Advisor, and can I speak to them on the phone before anything is booked?
would_share_with: My husband, with the who-pays paragraph, the Smartraveller section and the registry questions marked
My daughter, to ask whether the other family would rather do it at home, and to say let's ring them

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk through dates, islands or a wedding at home, a Wedded Advisor is happy to start the conversation.
cta_reaction.why: 'Start the conversation' suits me, and the fee in writing and AUD quotes reassure me. I'd click if I knew it meant a phone call with a real, named person, and some idea of who looks after the family over there.

top_3_changes: Add a short paragraph for older or less mobile guests in the Samoa section: flights, inter-island transfers, seating in a fale, travel insurance and medical cover (dengue), framed as questions to ask rather than invented details.

Next to the cyclone line or the Wedded Advisor line, say plainly what happens after you click (a phone call with a named person) and how weather postponements and deposits are handled, or list them as questions to ask.
Trim the museum and UNESCO detail in the mats sections so the practical planning tips (mat handling, umu, dress note) stand out sooner.
